Chemistry experiment · October 2026

Can an agent improve
the way it works?

Let an agent revise its own workflow. Test each change. Keep what works, and use the results to guide the next revision.

RSI is a method for improving an agent’s workflow. This experiment uses Claude Sonnet 5.5 in native Claude Code on two chemistry tasks.

Read the evidence

The first round starts with public task instructions. Later rounds also use scores and traces from this experiment.

Animation explains the process; it does not simulate experimental results. Instructions and Hooks show actual edits from this run in plain English. Other components show possible edits, not tested candidates.

What can change?

The harness is the guidance and support around the model: instructions, skills, helper tools, MCP tools, lifecycle hooks and task-local memory. The selected version adds a checklist, a checking tool and a one-shot stop hook.

What stays fixed?

Claude Sonnet 5.5 (high), the native Claude Code conversation and tool loop, the chemistry tasks, their experimental budgets, and the official scoring rules.

What makes it recursive?

An accepted change becomes the starting point for the next proposal. Every tested change leaves evidence for the next round, even when it is discarded.

The keep rule

Fixed before the run. Each candidate gets one screening trial per task, then two more unless it clearly fails against a working parent. A candidate is kept when its posterior probability of beating the parent is at least 0.8. A difference of one trial in six is treated as noise: it wins only if the candidate is also simpler or at least 15% cheaper. Before any trial, an automatic gate (format, leakage scan, offline smoke tests) and a critic must pass, with up to three repairs.

    What changed in each round

    A method beyond one model.

    The experiment separates task execution from workflow revision. All model roles in this run used Claude Sonnet 5.5. The controller talks to runtimes through adapters; other models need their own adapter and evaluation.

    Inspired by Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement. This is our own selection protocol, not a reproduction of the full paper.
